name: Sword of Ares (Artifact)
body:
Aura strong transmutation; CL 20th; Slot none; Weight 8 lbs.

DESCRIPTION

This imposing +3 vorpal shortsword radiates with the essence of battle, embodying the raw power and indomitable will of Ares. The blade is forged from an otherworldly metal, bearing intricate engravings depicting scenes of ancient and future battles.

When engaged in battle, the sword’s wielder gains a +1 sacred bonus to saving throws and Intimidate checks, and is immune to the frightened condition.

The wielder can cast haste once per day and power word kill once per day. Doing so requires a standard action that doesn’t provoke an attack of opportunity.

If the wielder is a cleric, warpriest, oracle, or champion (paladin) of Ares, they gain the following additional benefits:

Three times per day, after the wielder makes a successful attack against a target, they can use a swift action to force the target to make a DC 20 Strength check. On a failed save, the target is pushed back 15 feet and knocked prone.

Whenever the wielder scores a critical hit, the target must make a DC 20 Fortitude save. On a failed save, the target takes an additional 4d6 damage and is stunned for 1 round. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and is not stunned.

Each creature that starts its turn within 10 feet of the unsheathed, wielded sword must make a successful DC 20 Will save or be compelled to attack a randomly determined creature it can see other than the wielder. If there is no eligible creature within its reach, the creature uses its movement to close on the nearest creature and attack. A creature that makes its saving throw is immune to this ability for 24 hours.

The Sword of Ares is a weapon of great power and primal rage, carrying a curse that gradually corrupts the mind and soul of its wielder. If a wielder’s alignment is anything other than chaotic evil, they take 8d10 damage when they hold the sword for the first time. Over time, the sword’s owner becomes consumed by insatiable bloodlust, shifting their alignment towards chaos and evil. At the end of every seven days, the sword’s owner must make a DC 38 Will save. On a failed save, the owner’s alignment shifts one step closer to chaotic evil (as dictated by the GM). The curse can only be broken through a powerful ritual conducted in a temple dedicated to Ares, requiring the sacrifice of a worthy foe and the successful completion of a perilous quest (as determined by the GM). If the cursed creature no longer owns the sword, the creature returns to its original alignment in 2d20 + 30 days.

DESTRUCTION

If no wars occur on the Material Plane for thirteen consecutive months, the sword crumbles to dust.
